item.title: performOutbox reports done/failed even when the outcome write fails, leaving the record stuck in 'performing'

work.summary:
Problem: after performing an effect, performOutbox (packages/appboundry-host/src/transactions.ts) wrote the outcome with a version-guarded put. If that put threw, it only called warn() and still returned next.state ('done' or 'failed'). The record stayed 'performing' with attempts incremented, but callers took the return value as recorded. recoverOutbox (host.ts 521-523) counted it as performed. After OUTBOX_PERFORMING_STALE_MS (300 s) the record became recoverable again and the effect was re-run, including effects that had failed, which only an operator is supposed to retry.

Fix (transactions.ts only):
- The outcome write is now attempted up to a new bound, OUTBOX_OUTCOME_WRITE_ATTEMPTS = 3.
- After a failed write the record is re-read. If the write actually landed (same state and updatedAt; only the acknowledgement was lost), the recorded state is returned.
- If the record is still our unchanged 'performing' claim (same __version), the write is tried again.
- Otherwise it warns and returns 'skipped' instead of 'done'/'failed'. 'skipped' is an existing return value, so callers need no changes and never count an unrecorded effect as done or failed.
- The doc comment states that 'done' and 'failed' are reported only once recorded.
- No host.ts change: retryOutbox already re-reads the persisted record.

Test: new packages/appboundry-host/test/outbox-outcome.test.ts uses an in-memory store whose nth transaction can fail. It covers four cases:
- a done outcome that cannot be recorded is reported 'skipped' and stays 'performing', with a warning;
- the same for a failed outcome;
- a transient outcome-write failure is retried and records done with its result and attempts 1;
- the normal path still reports 'done'.
Against the original code three of the four failed. The first run expected 'unrecorded'; the done and failed cases then returned 'done'/'failed', and the retry case left the record 'performing'. I then changed those expectations to 'skipped'. I did not re-run against the original code after that change, but the original returns 'done'/'failed' in those cases, so the first two would still fail; the retry case was unaffected by the change.

With the fix:
- the new test passes, as do the existing transactional-effects.test.ts and transactions.test.ts;
- the build (tsc -b) succeeds.

After OUTBOX_PERFORMING_STALE_MS (300 s) the record became recoverable again and the effect was re-run, including effects that had failed, which only an operator is supposed to retry.

Fix (transactions.ts only):
- The outcome write is now attempted up to a new bound, OUTBOX_OUTCOME_WRITE_ATTEMPTS = 3.
- After a failed write the record is re-read. If the write actually landed (same state and updatedAt; only the acknowledgement was lost), the recorded state is returned.
- If the record is still our unchanged 'performing' claim (same __version), the write is tried again.
- Otherwise it warns and returns 'skipped' instead of 'done'/'failed'. 'skipped' is an existing return value, so callers need no changes and never count an unrecorded effect as done or failed.
- The doc comment states that 'done' and 'failed' are reported only once recorded.
- No host.ts change: retryOutbox already re-reads the persisted record.

Test: new packages/appboundry-host/test/outbox-outcome.test.ts uses an in-memory store whose nth transaction can fail. It covers four cases:
- a done outcome that cannot be recorded is reported 'skipped' and stays 'performing', with a warning;
- the same for a failed outcome;
- a transient outcome-write failure is retried and records done with its result and attempts 1;
- the normal path still reports 'done'.
Against the original code three of the four failed. The first run expected 'unrecorded'; the done and failed cases then returned 'done'/'failed', and the retry case left the record 'performing'. I then changed those expectations to 'skipped'. I did not re-run against the original code after that change, but the original returns 'done'/'failed' in those cases, so the first two would still fail; the retry case was unaffected by the change.

With the fix:
- the new test passes, as do the existing transactional-effects.test.ts and transactions.test.ts;
- the build (tsc -b) succeeds.","tests":["packages/appboundry-host/test/outbox-outcome.test.ts","packages/appboundry-host/test/transactions.test.ts","packages/appboundry-host/test/transactional-effects.test.ts"]}
data.rationale: The fix is in place; the new test failed before it and passes after it, the related suites pass, and the build succeeds.
